result.narrative:
Intel Corporation sits at the edge of the Watch band with a score of 20.7, driven entirely by news; the underlying payment record is pristine with zero days past due and no overdue or review evidence on file. The buyer's own trade performance gives no cause for concern, and the bulk of recent headlines about Intel are neutral-to-positive, covering new foundry customers and stock gains.

The Watch classification rests on a single severity-3 item: a Reuters headline reporting a shareholder lawsuit filed after a 29% stock plunge, weighted at 20.7 and accounting for the entire score. The adjudicator agreed with the formula's mechanics but flagged caveats, noting the article is a bare two-line wire notice with no detail on the lawsuit's substance or credit relevance, that shareholder suits following stock drops are a routine and often opportunistic occurrence for large-cap names, and that the rest of the recent news flow is positive and uncorroborative of distress. The score is only 0.7 points above the Healthy threshold, meaning this one headline is effectively the sole reason the buyer is not in the Healthy band.

Given the probability of default (0.1072) remains well within appetite against the 0.25 target, the recommendation is to maintain the current limit of $7,000,000 with no change in exposure.

The position would improve to Healthy with very little movement - the news item's weighting will decay over its 365-day half-life, and absent any further negative items the buyer would fall back below the Watch threshold. Conversely, the buyer would move toward High Risk only if payment performance deteriorated to around 38 days past due or if additional negative news raised the weighted score by roughly 29.3 points.
